title: Texas Instruments Stock Is Down 16% From Its 52-Week High. Is It a Buy?
author: John Ballard
description: Texas Instruments shares have declined 16% from their 52-week high despite strong Q2 earnings (23% revenue growth, 52% EPS growth) and doubled data center revenue. The stock sell-off was driven by soft Q3 guidance below analyst expectations, though management attributes this to timing of price increases rather than weak demand. The company benefits from AI infrastructure buildout, strong industrial demand, and offers an attractive 2.1% dividend yield with 22 consecutive years of increases.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite recent stock decline, the article highlights strong fundamentals including 23% revenue growth, 52% EPS growth, doubled data center revenue, broad-based industrial demand growth (30% YoY), solid automotive growth, competitive manufacturing advantages, and an attractive dividend yield of 2.1% with 22 consecutive years of increases. Soft Q3 guidance is attributed to timing of price increases rather than demand weakness, and management expects stronger results in Q4. The company is well-positioned to benefit from AI infrastructure investment.
